boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Mies Campus spaces where Illinois Tech students can study, make, play, exercise, record media, or meet—with access details grounded in university sources.

cards.title: Make MTCC Your Between-Class Base
cards.subtitle: Study, meet, play, or catch a campus program in the student center
cards.notes: Use the wireless study areas between classes, then check the building’s meeting rooms and event spaces when your group needs more structure.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose student hub combining informal work areas, recreation, organization offices, dining, and programmed events.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech identifies MTCC as a student-focused facility with wireless study areas, meeting and event rooms, student-organization offices, table tennis, pool, performances, lectures, and social events.
cards.access_notes: Campus-center facilities and programs have activity-specific rules; verify room reservations and event access before arriving.

cards.title: Book the Room Before the Group Chat Spirals
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms for collaborative work inside Galvin Library
cards.notes: Reserve up to 14 days ahead for a team session, and use the Group Study or Research Help desk when the start time is less than three hours away.
cards.short_summary: A practical option for project teams that need a defined room rather than open library seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Galvin Library provides group study and conference rooms for Illinois Tech students; reservations may last 30 minutes to two hours and can be made up to 14 days ahead.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to Illinois Tech students and subject to reservation limits; short-notice reservations must be made in person.

cards.title: Turn a Presentation Into a Production
cards.subtitle: A bookable second-floor studio for recording and streaming
cards.notes: Book a studio session before recording a presentation, interview, or stream, then review the linked studio guide for equipment and use rules.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated content-production room that moves media work out of noisy residence or common areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech says students, staff, and faculty can book GLaMS for video production, sound recording and editing, and streaming using its basic production tools.
cards.access_notes: Located on Galvin Library’s second floor next to the elevator; advance booking and compliance with studio rules are required.

cards.title: Pair Group Study With Academic Backup
cards.subtitle: Tutoring and collaborative space in Galvin Library 007
cards.notes: Check the current tutoring schedule, make an appointment when needed, and use the group-study space to continue working through the material together.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered learning space where peer tutoring, reviews, workshops, and group work meet.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Resource Center in Galvin Library 007 offers peer tutoring, exam reviews, workshops, limited peer advising, and group study spaces for Illinois Tech students.
cards.access_notes: Services are for current Illinois Tech students; consult the current appointment schedule because semester availability can change.

cards.entity_name: Janet and Craig Duchossois Idea Shop
cards.title: Move the Project Off the Screen
cards.subtitle: Flexible project space on Kaplan Institute’s ground level
cards.notes: Bring an early project concept here for collaborative work, and confirm training or supervision requirements before planning to use fabrication equipment.
cards.short_summary: An applied-project environment connecting open teamwork areas with prototyping and computing resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech describes the Duchossois Idea Shop as containing rapid-prototyping labs, computer resources, collaborative teaming areas, and flexible open spaces in Kaplan Institute.
cards.access_notes: Located on Kaplan Institute’s ground level; equipment use may require authorization, training, or project-specific access.

cards.title: Prototype Where the Tools Already Are
cards.subtitle: Kaplan Institute fabrication space with digital and hand tools
cards.notes: Match your prototype to the available 3D printers, CNC mills, electronics stations, or hand tools, then verify required training before scheduling work.
cards.short_summary: A named fabrication facility for turning designs into physical prototypes with several tool types in one place.
cards.evidence_claim: The university lists 3D printers, CNC mills, electronics workstations, and hand-fabrication tools in the Grainger Maker Space at Kaplan Institute.
cards.access_notes: Tool access is not described as unrestricted; verify eligibility, training, supervision, and equipment availability before use.

cards.title: Take the Break Below Street Level
cards.subtitle: Bowling, console games, and tabletop recreation on campus
cards.notes: Check the current operating notice before heading downstairs, then choose from bowling, console games, air hockey, billiards, or table tennis.
cards.short_summary: A subterranean recreation venue offering multiple social activities without requiring students to leave campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech documents The BOG as an on-campus gathering space with an eight-lane bowling alley, console and arcade games, billiards, foosball, air hockey, table tennis, and performances.
cards.access_notes: The university page says The BOG is closed for summer 2026 and will resume normal operations in fall; confirm reopening and event access.

cards.title: Find the Campus Gaming Room
cards.subtitle: Casual and competitive play inside MTCC
cards.notes: Look for casual gaming nights or student events before visiting, and contact Illinois Tech Esports if you want team or tournament information.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated MTCC gaming facility supporting both organized competition and lower-pressure community play.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech states that the Esports and Digital Arts Center opened in MTCC in 2018 and supports connection through tournaments and casual gaming nights.
cards.access_notes: Event and workstation availability can vary; consult Illinois Tech Esports for current hours, participation rules, and scheduled activities.

cards.title: Use the Campus as Your Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Drop-in fitness, courts, swimming, classes, and intramurals
cards.notes: Check the athletics schedule for open-gym or pool availability, then bring the required campus identification and gear for your chosen activity.
cards.short_summary: The main campus option for students seeking individual exercise, informal games, fitness classes, or intramural play.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech says every student has access to Keating’s facilities, fitness classes, intramural leagues, and tournaments; open swimming, fitness, and gym activities are also documented.
cards.access_notes: Facility, pool, class, and open-gym schedules can change for teams, breaks, holidays, and events; verify current access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: George J. Kacek Hall Study Lounges
cards.title: Use the Quiet Side of the Floor
cards.subtitle: North-side residential study lounges with downtown views
cards.notes: If you live in Kacek Hall, take focused work to the north-side study lounge and leave the south-side social lounge for conversation and breaks.
cards.short_summary: Purpose-built residential study areas separated from the building’s social lounges by floor and orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech states that each Kacek Hall floor has two large lounges, with study lounges on the north side and social lounges on the south side.
cards.access_notes: This is a residential-hall amenity; use is intended for authorized Kacek Hall residents and their permitted guests.
